A LILLE SPOT OF BOTHER
Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian.
Lille’s winner came from a similarly unlikely source of goals for the French side, with Aleksandar Pavlovic popping up to score a hilarious own goal that left his Bayern teammates giving him the collective stink-eye as he sank to his knees, head in hands in the traditional mea culpa style. Having seen Ethan Mbappé played clean through courtesy of a lightning-fast Lille counterattack, Pavlovic sprinted back towards his own team’s goal like a cheating spouse who’s just realised they left their phone unlocked on the coffee table. Although his panicked chase looked to be in vain, the German hit pay-dirt when Mbappé rolled his low shot past Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, only to see it rebound off the foot of the post. Cue Pavlovic, who accidentally stabbed the ball into the gaping goal as he attempted what appeared to be the routine task of putting it out for a corner.
While Pavlovic’s own goal was definitely the funniest Bayern have scored in recent memory, it certainly wasn’t the most embarrassing. That dubious honour goes to assorted club blazers including Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Uli Hoeness and Jan-Christian Dreesen, who have publicly questioned whether Musiala is worth the astronomical wages he is paid, given his struggles with knack and recent diagnosis with a treatable neurological disorder. Rummenigge even went so far as to suggest that if the 23-year-old does not return to top form, the remaining four years of his contract would “no longer be justifiable” and suggested a pay cut might be in order. Asked about this tone-deaf and decidedly mercenary invasion of his teammate’s medical privacy by club officials, Joshua Kimmich gave his superiors both barrels. “What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated in public,” he harrumphed. “It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it’s not bigger than a person. That’s an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like.” Neither is the shame of being second in the Bundesliga while languishing in 15th place in Bigger Cup Monster Group, but don’t expect anyone in the club boardroom to volunteer to trim their wages accordingly.
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE
Join Will Unwin from 8pm for hot Big Vase action, including Sunderland 2-1 Jagiellonia, Torreense 1-1 Celtic and Crystal Palace 1-1 Real Sociedad, plus reaction from Celta Vigo 0-1 Bournemouth, Brighton 3-0 Universitatea Craoiva and Hearts 0-3 Monaco.
QUOTE OF THE DAY
“Stability in a company is having standards. Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough. We have players who are here for four years, [who] can’t speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language. For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English” – Oliver Glasner puts his Nottingham Forest squad’s linguistic skills on blast.
FOOTBALL DAILY LETTERS
 
 I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner.
 
 The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis.
If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Mike Wilner. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

ביירן מינכן המשיכה את התקופה המאכזבת שלה עם הפסד 2-1 לליל במסגרת האירופית, כשהיא מופיעה בסגל חסר במיוחד עקב מכת פציעות שמאלצת שחקנים לשгра תפקידים לא להם. השיא במשחק הגיע כאשר הקשר אלכסנדר פבלוביץ' כבש שער עצמי משעשע ומביך, לאחר שניסה להרחיק כדור שפגע בקורה בעקבות מתפרצת מהירה של המארחת הצרפתית.

לצד התוצאות המקצועיות המאכזבות, המועדון ספג ביקורת פנימית קשה מצד שחקנים כמו יוזואה קימיך. זאת בעקבות התבטאויות פומביות של בכירים בהנהלה, דוגמת קרל-היינץ רומיניגה ואולי הנס, שפקפקו בצידוק לשכרו של ג'מאל מוסיאלה על רקע מאבקו בבעיות רפואיות. השחקנים הגדירו את הפגיעה בפרטיות הרפואית של חברם לקבוצה כקו אדום ואבסולוטי שאינו הולם את הערכים של ביירן מינכן.
